title: fix(data-objectstack,plugin-detail): concurrent record reads and explain questions share one request (objectui#11699)
body:
Part of #11699

Stays open on the card: `RecordDetailView`'s sequential `?populate=` re-read of the record when `objectDef` changes identity. Removing it needs `RecordDetailView.tsx`, which is held by objectui#11695's claim.

Clause-②: no

## What this does

Opening a record page sent `GET /api/v1/data/OBJ/ID` twice at once and `POST /api/v1/security/explain` four times. Measured, both duplications come from concurrent callers of one shared source. So the in-flight request is shared at those two sources, and neither host page is edited.

- **`@object-ui/data-objectstack`: `ObjectStackAdapter.findOne` shares an in-flight read** keyed by resource + id + params. `find`'s sharing code moved into one private helper, `shareInFlight`, that both methods now call; `find`'s behaviour is unchanged (its own pin is in the new test file). The entry is dropped when the read settles, so this is not a response cache. A rejection reaches every caller that shared it and is not remembered. A write through the adapter (`emitMutation`, which every create / update / delete / bulk / batch write goes through) drops the pending `findOne` reads of the resource it wrote, so a read asked after a save is never answered by one sent before it.
- **`@object-ui/plugin-detail`: `useRecordEditable` shares an unanswered question.** A pending map sits beside `verdictCache`, keyed the same way (principal, object, record, operation). A question whose record changes while it is pending is removed from the map, so the re-ask is a fresh request. A principal change empties the map, in `retainForPrincipal`, where `verdictCache` is cleared.

## Measurement: who sent the duplicates

Environment: objectstack `main` at `299a2c62`, the showcase app (`objectstack dev --seed-admin --fresh`, own port, temporary SQLite). The console is a production `vite build` of this branch, served by `vite preview` with `/api` proxied to that backend. Chromium headless 1440x900, seeded admin, full reload of a `showcase_task` record page. Requests were counted with Playwright `request` / `requestfinished` events, 4 runs per build.

| per reload | base `5a2a6ab` | this branch (`1c5b67b` source) |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_task/ID` | 2, concurrent | 1 |
| `POST /api/v1/security/explain`, `update` | 2, concurrent | 1 |
| `POST /api/v1/security/explain`, `delete` | 2, concurrent | 1 |
| `GET /api/v1/data/showcase_task?populate=…&top=1&filter=…` | 2, sequential | 2, sequential (see below) |
| all API requests | 44, 43, 43, 43 | 40, 40, 40, 40 |

The callers were named from one instrumented, unminified build. The instrumentation was reverted before anything was committed (`git diff HEAD` empty, marker count 0 in all four files).

- **Both `GET .../ID` come from `DetailView`'s load effect inside `record:details`**, from one `DetailView` instance. The effect re-runs because `RecordDetailsRenderer` builds a new `sections` array on every render, and the re-run happens while the first read is still on the wire. That read has no `$expand`, because the highlights strip's fields are de-duplicated out of the body. Sharing at `findOne` absorbs it.
- **The explain requests are 2 distinct questions, each asked twice.** `RecordDetailView` asks `update` and `delete`. `record:details`' `DetailView` asks the same two about 20 to 35 ms later, while the first answers are still pending. The principal was the same for all four, because permissions had loaded before the page mounted. Sharing in `useRecordEditable` absorbs it.
- **The `?populate=` pair is `RecordDetailView`'s own record read**, `findOne` with `$expand`, not a list. It is sent again after the first one settled, because `objectDef` arrives as a new object. Requests that are sequential cannot be shared in flight, so this pair is what keeps the card open. See acceptance note 1.

### The PM's mechanism assumptions, as measured

1. The record read: "two callers of `findOne`" is falsified in detail. It is ONE caller, `DetailView`, whose effect runs again while its first read is pending. The predicted remedy holds: the calls are concurrent on one adapter with the same key, and sharing at `findOne` absorbs them.
2. The explain probe: confirmed, 2 questions asked by 2 hosts. The clearing on a principal change lives in the hook's own `retainForPrincipal`. `purgeSignedOutClientCaches` is in `@object-ui/auth` and does not reach this module-scope map.
3. Hosts stay out: every in-scope duplicate is concurrent and goes through the same adapter or the same module, so neither host is touched. The only duplicate that sharing cannot absorb is the sequential `?populate=` re-read. It is a host's own sequential call, and it stays open on the card (acceptance note 1).
4. No new import enters the record page's module graph: neither source file gains an import.

## Tests

- `packages/data-objectstack/src/findOne.inflightShare-11699.test.ts` (new, 7 tests). This test runs the real adapter and the real client over a transport that holds each request until the test answers it. It covers: one GET for two concurrent calls; a new GET after settle; a different id, resource or params is not merged; a rejection is the same error for both callers (`httpStatus` 500, `code` `INTERNAL_ERROR`) and the next call asks again; a write to the resource makes the next read ask again; a write to another resource does not; `find` still shares.
- `packages/plugin-detail/src/useRecordEditable.inflightShare-11699.test.tsx` (new, 5 tests). The explain endpoint holds each request. It covers: two mounts send one POST and both show the verdict; distinct questions are not merged; a fail-open answer is shared but not remembered; a data change while pending makes the re-ask a fresh request; a principal change empties the map, so an unknown-principal ask after it does not join one from before.
- `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.recordOpenRequests-11699.test.tsx` (new, the integration pin). It mounts the real `RecordDetailView` with a showcase-shaped record page over the real adapter and the real hook. It releases held requests in the order the measurement saw, then counts: record `GET .../ID` is 1, and each of the 2 distinct explain questions is asked once. This is a test-only addition to app-shell, beside the host and outside the claim's file surface. `RecordDetailView.tsx` itself is untouched.

Runs (from the worktree root, through the shared verify lock):

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/data-objectstack/ packages/plugin-detail/`: `Test Files 321 passed | 1 skipped (322)`, `Tests 3470 passed | 8 skipped (3478)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=3 packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView`: `Test Files 42 passed (42)`, `Tests 257 passed (257)`. These are the host suites objectui#11713 once broke, plus the new pin.
- The consumer suites of both sources (every test file outside the two packages that names `useRecordEditable`, `__clearRecordEditableCache` or `security/explain`, or constructs `ObjectStackAdapter`): `Test Files 52 passed (52)`, `Tests 445 passed (445)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run type-check`: both `Done`. `--listFiles` shows both new test files in those programs. `packages/app-shell`: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exit 0 at `d1d1e87`, and `--listFiles` includes the new pin. These ran after the closure build `turbo run build --filter="@object-ui/app-shell^..."` (28/28 tasks).
- Lint: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/data-objectstack --filter @object-ui/plugin-detail run lint` reports 0 errors. Each touched source has the same warning count as at `5a2a6ab` (`index.ts` 123, `useRecordEditable.ts` 1), and both new test files have 0. For app-shell, `eslint --format json` on the one added file reports 1 file, 0 errors, 0 warnings. That is a declared narrowing: no other app-shell file changed, and `eslint.config.js` has no type-aware parser options (`projectService` / `parserOptions.project`).

## Ablations

Each ablation mutated committed `HEAD` (`1c5b67b`) through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode. The anchor hit exactly once, the blob changed, and the restore was proven by blob == HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`. Vitest resolves all three packages to `src` through `vitest.config.mts` aliases, so no `dist` was involved.

1. `findOne`'s sharing removed (`return this.shareInFlight(this.inflightFindOnes, …)` replaced by a direct `readOne`): 5 red. These are the four `findOne` share pins, plus the integration pin with `expected … to have a length of 1 but got 2`, which is the measured double GET.
2. The explain in-flight map removed (`if (pending) return pending.answer;` replaced): 3 red. The integration pin received `update: 2, delete: 2`, which is the measured four explains.
3. The write drop removed: only "a write to the resource … makes the next read ask again" is red.
4. The map clear on a principal change removed: only the principal-change pin is red.
5. The removal of a staled question from the map undone: only the data-change pin is red.

## Gates (exit codes captured before any pipe)

At `1078df3` (after merging `main` at `d39ac2e` and correcting the changeset prose): `check:changeset-claims` 0 · `check:pending-changeset-literals` 0 · `check-changeset-no-major` 0 · `check-changeset-presence` 0 (`5 source file(s) of 3 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)`) · `check-changeset-overwrite` 0 · `check:control-bytes` 0 · `check:new-line-citations` 0 (`VERDICT … 0 new citation(s)`).

At `d1d1e87`, and still standing: `check:vi-mock-specifiers` 0 · `check:vi-mock-inherit` 0 · `check:vi-mock-override-shape` 0 · `check:test-path-roots` 0 · `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the 7 paths: `NOT GOVERNED`, exit 0. The tests and ablations above were run at `d1d1e87` and its source, and they stand at `1078df3`. All six non-changeset files of this change have the same blob at both heads. The only file that differs outside the merge is the changeset. Every file the merge brought in equals `d39ac2e`, and none of them names the record page, `findOne` or `useRecordEditable`.

NOT MEASURED: `check:readme-exports`, reason: it needs every package built, and it judges only the import bindings a README writes, while the README edit here adds a prose bullet and no import. `check:doc-snippets`, reason: no code fence was added. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` and the full `pnpm test` farm are left to CI.

## Declaration delta

`ObjectStackAdapter` in `dist/index.d.ts` gains three private member names (`inflightFindOnes`, `shareInFlight`, `readOne`) and a JSDoc paragraph on `findOne`. No export, public member, prop, type member or i18n key changes. `useRecordEditable`'s new code is module-private. The changeset declares `patch` for both packages (`.changeset/11699-record-open-shared-reads.md`). Its prose claims only what was measured: the same record read is no longer sent twice at once, and the page's own `$expand` re-read is named as unchanged.

## Acceptance notes

- **The record is still read 3 times per open, as 2 different requests, so this PR is `Part of #11699`.** `DetailView` reads `GET .../ID` once (shared now). `RecordDetailView` reads `?populate=` twice in sequence, re-reading when `objectDef` changes identity. That pair is the page's own `$expand` record read, not a list, so the card's Done-when (one `GET` of the record per open) still covers it. The second read is sent after the first settles, so no in-flight sharing can absorb it. Removing it means an edit to `RecordDetailView.tsx`, which waits behind objectui#11695's claim.
- `DetailView` inside `record:details` reads the record itself while the page's record (`ctx.data`) is still loading, in parallel to the page's own read. This is a host-coordination question, not a sharing one, because the two requests carry different params.
- `RecordDetailsRenderer` builds a new `sections` array on every render, so `DetailView`'s load effect re-runs on unrelated re-renders. That is the root of the double GET, now absorbed by sharing. The schema read it repeats is served by the metadata cache.
- `find` has no write drop. The same staleness window `findOne` now closes is still open for lists. This is an inference, not reproduced.
- Measured and left alone, because they are not record reads: `GET /api/v1/runtime/config` and `GET /api/v1/auth/get-session` each go out twice, in sequence, on every reload (4 of 4 runs, both builds).
